Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 27.

(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification/provision of information regarding women victims of violence; employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence whose education has been interrupted; and

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PALOPO CITY
NUMBER 5 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, among others Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Trafficking in Persons, and Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
The Regional Government prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as regulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. The Basic Services referred to, one of which is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.
On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps in order to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children. The causes among others are the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from actions to prevent acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society.
Our hope is that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

NUMBER 5 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, among others Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Trafficking in Persons, and Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
The Regional Government prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as regulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. The Basic Services referred to, one of which is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.
On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps in order to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children. The causes among others are the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from actions to prevent acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society.
Our hope is that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Article 23
Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, and it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 27.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PALOPO CITY
NUMBER 5 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, among others Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Trafficking in Persons, and Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
The Regional Government prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as regulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. The Basic Services referred to, one of which is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.
On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps in order to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children. The causes among others are the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from actions to prevent acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society.
Our hope is that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.
